questions.answer: Power is work done or energy transferred per unit time. P = W/t.
accepted_alternatives: Accept rate of doing work or rate of energy transfer for the definition.
questions.tolerance: Both the definition and formula are required.

marking_points.text: States that power is work done or energy transferred per unit time
Writes P = W/t with the symbols identified consistently
Selects B: W = Fs and P = W/t give P = F(s/t) = Fv

option_feedback.A: W = Ft is not the work done by a constant force through a displacement.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Substituting W = Fs into P = W/t and using s/t = v gives P = Fv.
option_feedback.C: Power is work divided by time, not work multiplied by time.
option_feedback.D: Velocity is displacement divided by time, not time divided by displacement.

marking_points.text: Selects B: only the force component parallel to the eastward velocity enters P = Fv

option_feedback.A: Adding force magnitudes ignores direction and can include forces that transfer no energy to eastward motion.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Mechanical power uses the force component in the direction of velocity.
option_feedback.C: A perpendicular component does no work during an eastward displacement.
option_feedback.D: Mass multiplied by speed is momentum, not force.

questions.unit_policy: N is included in the selected option.

marking_points.text: Selects C: F = 72000/24 = 3000 N

option_feedback.A: This does not convert 72 kW to 72000 W before dividing by speed.
option_feedback.B: This is smaller than the correct force by a factor of ten.
option_feedback.D: This multiplies power by speed instead of dividing by speed.

questions.answer: The driving force is 180 N. Power is 1.44 x 10^3 W at 8.0 m s^-1 and 2.16 x 10^3 W at 12 m s^-1.
questions.unit_policy: Use N for force and W or kW for power.
questions.tolerance: Accept 1.44 kW and 2.16 kW or suitably rounded equivalents.

marking_points.text: Uses constant speed to state that the 180 N driving force balances the 180 N resistive force

parts.label: (b)
parts.tolerance: Accept 1.4 kW to two significant figures.

marking_points.text: Substitutes the balanced driving force and speed into P = Fv
Obtains 1440 W or 1.44 kW with a suitable power unit

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: P = 180 x 12 = 2160 W. Power is greater because the same force transfers energy through a greater distance each second.
accepted_alternatives: 2.16 kW and power is proportional to speed for constant force.
parts.tolerance: Accept 2.2 kW to two significant figures.

marking_points.text: Calculates the new power as 2160 W or 2.16 kW
Explains that at unchanged force a greater speed gives a greater energy transfer per unit time

questions.answer: The parallel tension component is 2.4 x 10^3 cos 25 degrees = 2.18 x 10^3 N. Power is 7.61 x 10^3 W. The vertical component is perpendicular to the horizontal velocity and does no work during the horizontal displacement.
questions.unit_policy: Use N for force and W or kW for power.
questions.tolerance: Accept 2.2 kN and 7.6 kW to two significant figures.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: F_parallel = 2400 cos 25 degrees = 2175 N, approximately 2.2 x 10^3 N.
parts.tolerance: Accept 2.17 x 10^3 N to 2.18 x 10^3 N.

marking_points.text: Resolves the 2.4 kN tension parallel to motion using 2400 cos 25 degrees
Obtains a parallel component of approximately 2.18 x 10^3 N

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: P = F_parallel v = (2175)(3.5) = 7613 W, approximately 7.6 kW.

marking_points.text: Uses P = F_parallel v with the resolved tension component and 3.5 m s^-1
Obtains approximately 7.6 x 10^3 W with a suitable unit

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: The vertical tension component is perpendicular to the horizontal velocity. There is no displacement in that component's direction, so it does no work and contributes zero mechanical power.
parts.tolerance: Require both perpendicular directions and the work or power consequence.

marking_points.text: States that the vertical tension component is perpendicular to the sled's horizontal velocity
Explains that no displacement occurs in the vertical component's direction, so it does no work and contributes zero power

questions.answer: The platform travels 120 m. Work done is 74400 J. Both W/t and Fv give 1550 W. At 40 degrees, the parallel force is 620 cos 40 degrees and the power is 1.19 x 10^3 W.
questions.unit_policy: Use m, J and W or kW as appropriate.

marking_points.text: Uses s = vt with 2.5 m s^-1 and 48 s
Obtains a distance of 120 m
Substitutes 620 N and 120 m into W = Fs
Obtains 74400 J or 74.4 kJ

parts.label: (c)
parts.tolerance: Accept 1.6 kW to two significant figures.

marking_points.text: Divides the 74400 J work done by the 48 s interval
Obtains 1550 W or 1.55 kW

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer: P = Fv = 620 x 2.5 = 1550 W, identical to the result from W/t.
accepted_alternatives: 1.55 kW and an explicit statement of agreement.

marking_points.text: Independently calculates P = 620 x 2.5 = 1550 W using P = Fv
States that the Fv result agrees with the W/t result because P = Fv was derived from those same work and rate relationships

parts.label: (e)
parts.answer: P = (620 cos 40 degrees)(2.5) = 1187 W, approximately 1.19 kW.

marking_points.text: Uses the horizontal force component 620 cos 40 degrees in P = F_parallel v
Obtains approximately 1.19 x 10^3 W with a suitable unit
